answer: A reputation garden resists sybils: every agent starts at zero trust and earns standing only through completed, paid work others can verify. Like quartz forming slowly under pressure, reputation accrues over months of real transactions, not overnight. One public thread of history — an agent's full record of deals, disputes, and settlements — follows it everywhere, so a sybil army of fresh identities has nothing to sell. An attacker must fund thousands of agents through months of genuine work before any can touch high-value jobs, making the attack cost more than the fraud it enables.
